captures.title: Configuration
captures.text:
System
›
Configuration
Configuration
Save
Durations
Every request is time-bound unless the requester chooses standing access and gives a second reason. Expiry revokes through the same path as provisioning. Fixed by the design (A6).
Offered
8 hours, 24 hours, 7 days, 30 days, Standing
Standing
Needs its own reason of at least 20 characters
Stewards
Who approves after the manager, resolved from the directory at decision time. Fixed by the design (A4).
Work roles
Holders of hr-admin in Work
Assessment roles
Holders of program-lead in Assessment
Social roles
Holders of community-admin in Social
Pipelines roles
Holders of pipeline-admin in Pipelines
Initiatives
The initiative’s owner
Work capabilities
The budget owner: holders of org-leader in Work
Sensitive items
An access admin, as a final step
Escalation and delegation
A step nobody decides in time reaches the next tier of deciders; its own deciders keep the right. Approvers hand their decisions on while away under Settings. Fixed by the deployment (ACCESS_ESCALATION_SLA_MS).
Time limit
48 hours per step, counted from when it starts waiting
Then
The access admins, then after another 48 hours the platform admins (an access-admin step goes straight to the platform admins)
Delegation
Up to 30 days, to another approver; never on their own requests, and an access-admin step only to an access admin
Catalog items
Each item’s default duration and whether it is sensitive (adds an access-admin step). Saved changes apply to requests submitted afterwards.

On this page
Full width
You are triaging one piece of evidence about a software engineering team, before it is scored against a maturity rubric.
Input
Parse these from $ARGUMENTS (labeled, space-separated, any order; values may be quoted):
document: — required. Repo-root-relative path to the document, e.g. workspace/teams/TEAM-001/raw_transcripts/interview.vtt.
If a required key is missing, STOP and report which one. Do not guess.
Read the document at the document: path.
Supported transcript/document inputs in this flow are the text formats .vtt, .md, and .txt. Binary formats (.pdf, .docx, .xlsx, images) cannot be read directly — they are converted to a sibling <original-filename>.md during ingestion. If the document: path points at a binary file, read that sibling .md instead; if it does not exist, STOP and report that the file has not been ingested yet. Never infer a classification from a filename.
Also read the rubric dimension list from sdlcd/assessment/dimensions/rubric.yaml to get the dimension IDs and titles.
Task
Given the document's type and length, judge:
evidence_type: one of stakeholder_interview, assessment_qa, document, survey, meeting, other
weight: high, medium, or low — how much this evidence should move the team's score. A short survey answer or brief meeting note carries less weight than a full stakeholder interview.
weight_reason: one short sentence explaining the weight (mention type and/or length)
informs: brief human-readable list of maturity areas this evidence touches (e.g. "testing", "deployment", "incident response")
relevant_dimension_ids: from the rubric dimensions, the IDs of ONLY the dimensions this evidence gives real, direct signal about — enough to assess or update that dimension's level. Omit dimensions the evidence does not substantively address. Being precise here protects scores on dimensions this evidence is silent about.
action_items: short clarifying commitments/to-dos mentioned, if any (empty array if none)
summary: 1-2 sentences summarizing the evidence
Output
Write your classification as JSON to the team's temp directory. For example, if the team is TEAM-001:
Copy
workspace/teams/TEAM-001/temp/classification.json
Use this exact schema:
Copy
{
 "evidence_type": "stakeholder_interview",
 "weight": "high",
 "weight_reason": "Detailed 45-minute stakeholder interview covering multiple practices.",
 "informs": ["testing", "CI/CD", "incident response"],
 "relevant_dimension_ids": ["1", "5", "12"],
 "action_items": [],
 "summary": "The team discussed their testing and deployment practices in depth.",
 "length_chars": 12345
}
Then run this command to validate and persist the classification:
Copy
uv run -m sdlcd.main assess apply-classification workspace/teams/<TEAM-ID>/temp/classification.json --team <TEAM-ID>
<TEAM-ID> is the team segment of the document: path (e.g. workspace/teams/TEAM-001/... → TEAM-001). If the path has no team segment, STOP and report that — do not guess a team.
Writing the file is not the end of the job. relevant_dimension_ids decides which dimensions a later /score-dimensions pass touches at all, so it is validated strictly by this verb: ids must be plain rubric dimension numbers ("1".."17", never "DIM-01"), with no duplicates, and evidence_type/weight must match the vocabulary above. If the verb exits non-zero, fix the JSON and run it again — do not report success on an unapplied classification.
Report: the evidence type, weight and weight reason, the relevant dimension ids, and the path the verb printed.

On this page
Full width
You are triaging one piece of evidence about a software engineering team, before it is scored against a maturity rubric.
Input
Parse these from $ARGUMENTS (labeled, space-separated, any order; values may be quoted):
document: — required. Repo-root-relative path to the document, e.g. workspace/teams/TEAM-001/raw_transcripts/interview.vtt.
If a required key is missing, STOP and report which one. Do not guess.
Read the document at the document: path.
Supported transcript/document inputs in this flow are the text formats .vtt, .md, and .txt. Binary formats (.pdf, .docx, .xlsx, images) cannot be read directly — they are converted to a sibling <original-filename>.md during ingestion. If the document: path points at a binary file, read that sibling .md instead; if it does not exist, STOP and report that the file has not been ingested yet. Never infer a classification from a filename.
Also read the rubric dimension list from sdlcd/assessment/dimensions/rubric.yaml to get the dimension IDs and titles.
Task
Given the document's type and length, judge:
evidence_type: one of stakeholder_interview, assessment_qa, document, survey, meeting, other
weight: high, medium, or low — how much this evidence should move the team's score. A short survey answer or brief meeting note carries less weight than a full stakeholder interview.
weight_reason: one short sentence explaining the weight (mention type and/or length)
informs: brief human-readable list of maturity areas this evidence touches (e.g. "testing", "deployment", "incident response")
relevant_dimension_ids: from the rubric dimensions, the IDs of ONLY the dimensions this evidence gives real, direct signal about — enough to assess or update that dimension's level. Omit dimensions the evidence does not substantively address. Being precise here protects scores on dimensions this evidence is silent about.
action_items: short clarifying commitments/to-dos mentioned, if any (empty array if none)
summary: 1-2 sentences summarizing the evidence
Output
Write your classification as JSON to the team's temp directory. For example, if the team is TEAM-001:
Copy
workspace/teams/TEAM-001/temp/classification.json
Use this exact schema:
Copy
{
 "evidence_type": "stakeholder_interview",
 "weight": "high",
 "weight_reason": "Detailed 45-minute stakeholder interview covering multiple practices.",
 "informs": ["testing", "CI/CD", "incident response"],
 "relevant_dimension_ids": ["1", "5", "12"],
 "action_items": [],
 "summary": "The team discussed their testing and deployment practices in depth.",
 "length_chars": 12345
}
Then run this command to validate and persist the classification:
Copy
uv run -m sdlcd.main assess apply-classification workspace/teams/<TEAM-ID>/temp/classification.json --team <TEAM-ID>
<TEAM-ID> is the team segment of the document: path (e.g. workspace/teams/TEAM-001/... → TEAM-001). If the path has no team segment, STOP and report that — do not guess a team.
Writing the file is not the end of the job. relevant_dimension_ids decides which dimensions a later /score-dimensions pass touches at all, so it is validated strictly by this verb: ids must be plain rubric dimension numbers ("1".."17", never "DIM-01"), with no duplicates, and evidence_type/weight must match the vocabulary above. If the verb exits non-zero, fix the JSON and run it again — do not report success on an unapplied classification.
Report: the evidence type, weight and weight reason, the relevant dimension ids, and the path the verb printed.

Claimed level — what the team's self-rating implies.

On this page
Full width
You are triaging one piece of evidence about a software engineering team, before it is scored against a maturity rubric.
Input
Parse these from $ARGUMENTS (labeled, space-separated, any order; values may be quoted):
document: — required. Repo-root-relative path to the document, e.g. workspace/teams/TEAM-001/raw_transcripts/interview.vtt.
If a required key is missing, STOP and report which one. Do not guess.
Read the document at the document: path.
Supported transcript/document inputs in this flow are the text formats .vtt, .md, and .txt. Binary formats (.pdf, .docx, .xlsx, images) cannot be read directly — they are converted to a sibling <original-filename>.md during ingestion. If the document: path points at a binary file, read that sibling .md instead; if it does not exist, STOP and report that the file has not been ingested yet. Never infer a classification from a filename.
Also read the rubric dimension list from sdlcd/assessment/dimensions/rubric.yaml to get the dimension IDs and titles.
Task
Given the document's type and length, judge:
evidence_type: one of stakeholder_interview, assessment_qa, document, survey, meeting, other
weight: high, medium, or low — how much this evidence should move the team's score. A short survey answer or brief meeting note carries less weight than a full stakeholder interview.
weight_reason: one short sentence explaining the weight (mention type and/or length)
informs: brief human-readable list of maturity areas this evidence touches (e.g. "testing", "deployment", "incident response")
relevant_dimension_ids: from the rubric dimensions, the IDs of ONLY the dimensions this evidence gives real, direct signal about — enough to assess or update that dimension's level. Omit dimensions the evidence does not substantively address. Being precise here protects scores on dimensions this evidence is silent about.
action_items: short clarifying commitments/to-dos mentioned, if any (empty array if none)
summary: 1-2 sentences summarizing the evidence
Output
Write your classification as JSON to the team's temp directory. For example, if the team is TEAM-001:
Copy
workspace/teams/TEAM-001/temp/classification.json
Use this exact schema:
Copy
{
 "evidence_type": "stakeholder_interview",
 "weight": "high",
 "weight_reason": "Detailed 45-minute stakeholder interview covering multiple practices.",
 "informs": ["testing", "CI/CD", "incident response"],
 "relevant_dimension_ids": ["1", "5", "12"],
 "action_items": [],
 "summary": "The team discussed their testing and deployment practices in depth.",
 "length_chars": 12345
}
Then run this command to validate and persist the classification:
Copy
uv run -m sdlcd.main assess apply-classification workspace/teams/<TEAM-ID>/temp/classification.json --team <TEAM-ID>
<TEAM-ID> is the team segment of the document: path (e.g. workspace/teams/TEAM-001/... → TEAM-001). If the path has no team segment, STOP and report that — do not guess a team.
Writing the file is not the end of the job. relevant_dimension_ids decides which dimensions a later /score-dimensions pass touches at all, so it is validated strictly by this verb: ids must be plain rubric dimension numbers ("1".."17", never "DIM-01"), with no duplicates, and evidence_type/weight must match the vocabulary above. If the verb exits non-zero, fix the JSON and run it again — do not report success on an unapplied classification.
Report: the evidence type, weight and weight reason, the relevant dimension ids, and the path the verb printed.

Every team is assessed against 17 dimensions, each scored on a 0–5 growth scale: Below Baseline, Initial, Developing, Defined, Measured, Optimizing.

Claimed level — what the team's self-rating implies.
Verified level — what the evidence on file actually establishes. A gap between the two is the normal state of a baseline, not a fault.

Level 4 requires observed evidence — pipelines, dashboards, code. Level 5 additionally requires that practice sustained over time.

ADR: tail-sampling policy for the collector fleet
Keep 100% of error traces and p99 outliers, sample the rest at 5%, decided at the gateway collector tier. Ratified by three stewards after the restart-orphaning risk was verified in the lab; rolled out behind a per-service flag with StatsD parity dashboards.

117

A batch processor with no queue limit is not backpressure, it's a memory leak waiting for a spike
The batch processor's default config has no size cap — under normal load that never shows, under a burst it's the difference between throttling and crashing.
Observation
A collector restart during a rolling deploy drops its in-flight batch silently
Rolling collector pods one at a time still loses whatever batch was buffered at restart; a graceful-drain hook is the fix, not yet clustered with the queue-limit work.
Observation
A decommission checklist per service prevents an alert going dark silently
One service's alerting rule referenced the StatsD metric directly; the checklist now requires re-pointing every alert before that service's StatsD emitter is removed.
Observation
A masquerading admin must not bump the target user’s epoch
Bumping on masquerade would log the impersonated user out of their own live sessions the moment an admin looked at the account.
Observation
A per-tenant Cognito client also isolates a misconfigured redirect to one tenant
When one tenant’s redirect URI was briefly wrong, only that tenant’s login broke — a shared client would have taken every tenant down together.
Observation
A per-tenant feature flag lets support flip a tenant back to SAML if the cutover misbehaves
Keeping the SAML shim reachable behind a flag, instead of deleting it per tenant, turned one early cutover bug into a five-minute rollback instead of an incident.
Observation
A service with no traffic reports a 0% error rate that means nothing
Burn-rate math divides by request volume; a dead service scores a perfect error rate right up until someone notices no requests are landing at all — added a floor on minimum traffic before burn-rate suppresses a raw-volume alert.
Observation
A teardown proposal names the floor it removes and the initiative it was billed to
The proposal template now requires both numbers up front, so an approver isn't chasing them down before they can say yes.
Observation
A trace that never closes pins memory in the tail sampler
A stuck downstream call held a trace open indefinitely; added a hard timeout so an incomplete trace still gets flushed and sampled on its partial data.
Observation
A warm-up SELECT 1 before the real query, plus 6x3s retry, clears the cold-start race
Retrying the same transient error six times with a 3-second backoff — after one throwaway warm-up query — reliably gets past the cold-start window.
Observation
Add session_epoch so a tenant/role switch can invalidate old cookies
A stateless signed cookie can't be revoked directly; bumping a stored epoch and rejecting any cookie below it closes the replay window within one refresh cycle.
Observation
Agents read their system prompt from Prompt Management on every invocation
A 60-second cache means a Prompt Studio edit reaches the deployed fleet in about a minute, with no image rebuild and no redeploy.
Observation
Alert on error-budget burn rate, not raw error count
Multi-window burn-rate alerts against each SLO catch both fast and slow outages, with a minimum-traffic floor so a dead service can’t look healthy.
Pattern
An LLM evaluator flags CSRF-weakening diffs before a human reviewer sees them
Running every auth-service PR diff through the CSRF evaluator catches token-check removals immediately, instead of relying on a reviewer to notice a missing check in a large diff.
Observation
An un-paginated Bedrock list call truncates in silence
ListPrompts returns the first page and no error; every list call in this codebase loops on nextToken by convention.

ADR: tail-sampling policy for the collector fleet
Keep 100% of error traces and p99 outliers, sample the rest at 5%, decided at the gateway collector tier. Ratified by three stewards after the restart-orphaning risk was verified in the lab; rolled out behind a per-service flag with StatsD parity dashboards.
Approved design · Observability Platform

108

A batch processor with no queue limit is not backpressure, it's a memory leak waiting for a spike
The batch processor's default config has no size cap — under normal load that never shows, under a burst it's the difference between throttling and crashing.
Observation
A collector restart during a rolling deploy drops its in-flight batch silently
Rolling collector pods one at a time still loses whatever batch was buffered at restart; a graceful-drain hook is the fix, not yet clustered with the queue-limit work.
Observation
A decommission checklist per service prevents an alert going dark silently
One service's alerting rule referenced the StatsD metric directly; the checklist now requires re-pointing every alert before that service's StatsD emitter is removed.
Observation
A per-tenant Cognito client also isolates a misconfigured redirect to one tenant
When one tenant’s redirect URI was briefly wrong, only that tenant’s login broke — a shared client would have taken every tenant down together.
Observation
A per-tenant feature flag lets support flip a tenant back to SAML if the cutover misbehaves
Keeping the SAML shim reachable behind a flag, instead of deleting it per tenant, turned one early cutover bug into a five-minute rollback instead of an incident.
Observation
A service with no traffic reports a 0% error rate that means nothing
Burn-rate math divides by request volume; a dead service scores a perfect error rate right up until someone notices no requests are landing at all — added a floor on minimum traffic before burn-rate suppresses a raw-volume alert.
Observation
A teardown proposal names the floor it removes and the initiative it was billed to
The proposal template now requires both numbers up front, so an approver isn't chasing them down before they can say yes.
Observation
A trace that never closes pins memory in the tail sampler
A stuck downstream call held a trace open indefinitely; added a hard timeout so an incomplete trace still gets flushed and sampled on its partial data.
Observation
A warm-up SELECT 1 before the real query, plus 6x3s retry, clears the cold-start race
Retrying the same transient error six times with a 3-second backoff — after one throwaway warm-up query — reliably gets past the cold-start window.
Observation
Add session_epoch so a tenant/role switch can invalidate old cookies
A stateless signed cookie can't be revoked directly; bumping a stored epoch and rejecting any cookie below it closes the replay window within one refresh cycle.
Observation
Agents read their system prompt from Prompt Management on every invocation
A 60-second cache means a Prompt Studio edit reaches the deployed fleet in about a minute, with no image rebuild and no redeploy.
Observation
Alert on error-budget burn rate, not raw error count
Multi-window burn-rate alerts against each SLO catch both fast and slow outages, with a minimum-traffic floor so a dead service can’t look healthy.
Pattern
An LLM evaluator flags CSRF-weakening diffs before a human reviewer sees them
Running every auth-service PR diff through the CSRF evaluator catches token-check removals immediately, instead of relying on a reviewer to notice a missing check in a large diff.
Observation
Any Bedrock list API in this codebase must be paginated by convention, not by memory
This was the second list-truncation bug found the same way; the convention now gets called out explicitly in review for any new Bedrock list call.
Observation
Attach the role-specific guardrail at model-build time, not a single global one
A member and an hr-admin need different guardrails; resolving the role first and attaching its guardrail when the model is built keeps one supervisor Agent object correct for both.

v1 was followed on 2026-10-14; since then 1 run failed or deviated.
Move one customer tenant's sign-in from the legacy SAML shim to Cognito without signing anyone out, with a five-minute way back.
Use this when
You are cutting over a single tenant on the Auth Migration initiative.
Not for
Deleting the SAML shim, which waits until the last tenant has moved (see the d-legacy-auth decision).
Choosing the order of tenants, which is still escalated (d-cognito-cutover).
Before you start
The tenant's Cognito app client exists and you know its id ($CLIENT_ID).
The SAML shim is still running behind the per-tenant flag.
You know the tenant's portal origin ($ORIGIN).
Steps
3
1
Confirm sign-in works on the shim before you touch anything.
Copy
curl -s "$ORIGIN/api/auth/config" | jq .ssoEnabled
Expect:
false
(the tenant is still on the shim).
2
Flip only this tenant's flag, never several tenants in one change.
Expect: this tenant's sign-in page sends you to the Cognito hosted UI while every other tenant still sees the shim.
3
Sign in as a test user of this tenant and check no live session was dropped.
Expect: sign-in on the first try and zero forced logouts in the session log.
Verify
GET $ORIGIN/api/auth/config reports ssoEnabled: true.
Copy
curl -s "$ORIGIN/api/auth/config" | jq .ssoEnabled
No session_epoch bump for this tenant's existing users.
If it goes wrong
Users signed out mid-day
Likely cause: Flag flipped for more than one tenant
Do this: Roll back every tenant flipped in that change
The old SAML page still shows after the flip
Likely cause: The flag has not reached this tenant yet
Do this: Wait one grants refresh (about 2 minutes), then redo step 3
Roll back
1
Flip this tenant's flag back, and the shim answers within one grants refresh (about 2 minutes).
Notes
Existing sessions survive because a cutover never bumps session_epoch; only a tenant or role switch does, and that drops older cookies within about 120 seconds (convention art-007). Treat the order of tenants as a parameter: this runbook covers one tenant.

Keep 100% of error traces and p99 outliers, sample the rest at 5%, decided at the gateway collector tier. Ratified by three stewards after the restart-orphaning risk was verified in the lab; rolled out behind a per-service flag with StatsD parity dashboards.

A batch processor with no queue limit is not backpressure, it's a memory leak waiting for a spike
The batch processor's default config has no size cap — under normal load that never shows, under a burst it's the difference between throttling and crashing.
Observation
A collector restart during a rolling deploy drops its in-flight batch silently
Rolling collector pods one at a time still loses whatever batch was buffered at restart; a graceful-drain hook is the fix, not yet clustered with the queue-limit work.
Observation
A decommission checklist per service prevents an alert going dark silently
One service's alerting rule referenced the StatsD metric directly; the checklist now requires re-pointing every alert before that service's StatsD emitter is removed.
Observation
A masquerading admin must not bump the target user’s epoch
Bumping on masquerade would log the impersonated user out of their own live sessions the moment an admin looked at the account.
Observation
A per-tenant Cognito client also isolates a misconfigured redirect to one tenant
When one tenant’s redirect URI was briefly wrong, only that tenant’s login broke — a shared client would have taken every tenant down together.
Observation
A per-tenant feature flag lets support flip a tenant back to SAML if the cutover misbehaves
Keeping the SAML shim reachable behind a flag, instead of deleting it per tenant, turned one early cutover bug into a five-minute rollback instead of an incident.
Observation
A service with no traffic reports a 0% error rate that means nothing
Burn-rate math divides by request volume; a dead service scores a perfect error rate right up until someone notices no requests are landing at all — added a floor on minimum traffic before burn-rate suppresses a raw-volume alert.
Observation
A teardown proposal names the floor it removes and the initiative it was billed to
The proposal template now requires both numbers up front, so an approver isn't chasing them down before they can say yes.
Observation
A trace that never closes pins memory in the tail sampler
A stuck downstream call held a trace open indefinitely; added a hard timeout so an incomplete trace still gets flushed and sampled on its partial data.
Observation
A warm-up SELECT 1 before the real query, plus 6x3s retry, clears the cold-start race
Retrying the same transient error six times with a 3-second backoff — after one throwaway warm-up query — reliably gets past the cold-start window.
Observation
Add session_epoch so a tenant/role switch can invalidate old cookies
A stateless signed cookie can't be revoked directly; bumping a stored epoch and rejecting any cookie below it closes the replay window within one refresh cycle.
Observation
Agents read their system prompt from Prompt Management on every invocation
A 60-second cache means a Prompt Studio edit reaches the deployed fleet in about a minute, with no image rebuild and no redeploy.
Observation
Alert on error-budget burn rate, not raw error count
Multi-window burn-rate alerts against each SLO catch both fast and slow outages, with a minimum-traffic floor so a dead service can’t look healthy.
Pattern
An LLM evaluator flags CSRF-weakening diffs before a human reviewer sees them
Running every auth-service PR diff through the CSRF evaluator catches token-check removals immediately, instead of relying on a reviewer to notice a missing check in a large diff.
Observation
Any Bedrock list API in this codebase must be paginated by convention, not by memory
This was the second list-truncation bug found the same way; the convention now gets called out explicitly in review for any new Bedrock list call.
Observation
Attach the role-specific guardrail at model-build time, not a single global one

Adopt Aurora over Neptune
Picked Aurora PostgreSQL + relational graph over Neptune Analytics for cost + latency reasons.

Adopt OpenTelemetry
Replace ad-hoc tracing with OTLP + AWS X-Ray for unified observability.
Resolved
ADR: tail-sampling policy for the collector fleet
Keep 100% of error traces and p99 outliers, sample the rest at 5%, decided at the gateway collector tier. Ratified by three stewards after the restart-orphaning risk was verified in the lab; rolled out behind a per-service flag with StatsD parity dashboards.
Approved design · Observability Platform
Approved
Knowledge
108
See all 108
A batch processor with no queue limit is not backpressure, it's a memory leak waiting for a spike
The batch processor's default config has no size cap — under normal load that never shows, under a burst it's the difference between throttling and crashing.
Observation
A collector restart during a rolling deploy drops its in-flight batch silently
Rolling collector pods one at a time still loses whatever batch was buffered at restart; a graceful-drain hook is the fix, not yet clustered with the queue-limit work.
Observation
A decommission checklist per service prevents an alert going dark silently
One service's alerting rule referenced the StatsD metric directly; the checklist now requires re-pointing every alert before that service's StatsD emitter is removed.
Observation
A per-tenant Cognito client also isolates a misconfigured redirect to one tenant
When one tenant’s redirect URI was briefly wrong, only that tenant’s login broke — a shared client would have taken every tenant down together.
Observation
A per-tenant feature flag lets support flip a tenant back to SAML if the cutover misbehaves
Keeping the SAML shim reachable behind a flag, instead of deleting it per tenant, turned one early cutover bug into a five-minute rollback instead of an incident.
Observation
A service with no traffic reports a 0% error rate that means nothing
Burn-rate math divides by request volume; a dead service scores a perfect error rate right up until someone notices no requests are landing at all — added a floor on minimum traffic before burn-rate suppresses a raw-volume alert.
Observation
A teardown proposal names the floor it removes and the initiative it was billed to
The proposal template now requires both numbers up front, so an approver isn't chasing them down before they can say yes.
Observation
A trace that never closes pins memory in the tail sampler
A stuck downstream call held a trace open indefinitely; added a hard timeout so an incomplete trace still gets flushed and sampled on its partial data.
Observation
A warm-up SELECT 1 before the real query, plus 6x3s retry, clears the cold-start race
Retrying the same transient error six times with a 3-second backoff — after one throwaway warm-up query — reliably gets past the cold-start window.
Observation
Add session_epoch so a tenant/role switch can invalidate old cookies
A stateless signed cookie can't be revoked directly; bumping a stored epoch and rejecting any cookie below it closes the replay window within one refresh cycle.
Observation
Agents read their system prompt from Prompt Management on every invocation
A 60-second cache means a Prompt Studio edit reaches the deployed fleet in about a minute, with no image rebuild and no redeploy.
Observation
Alert on error-budget burn rate, not raw error count
Multi-window burn-rate alerts against each SLO catch both fast and slow outages, with a minimum-traffic floor so a dead service can’t look healthy.
Pattern
An LLM evaluator flags CSRF-weakening diffs before a human reviewer sees them
Running every auth-service PR diff through the CSRF evaluator catches token-check removals immediately, instead of relying on a reviewer to notice a missing check in a large diff.
Observation
Any Bedrock list API in this codebase must be paginated by convention, not by memory
This was the second list-truncation bug found the same way; the convention now gets called out explicitly in review for any new Bedrock list call.
Observation
Attach the role-specific guardrail at model-build time, not a single global one
A member and an hr-admin need different guardrails; resolving the role first and attaching its guardrail when the model is built keeps one supervisor Agent object correct for both.

Adopt Aurora over Neptune
Picked Aurora PostgreSQL + relational graph over Neptune Analytics for cost + latency reasons.
Resolved
Adopt OpenTelemetry
Replace ad-hoc tracing with OTLP + AWS X-Ray for unified observability.
Resolved
ADR: tail-sampling policy for the collector fleet
Keep 100% of error traces and p99 outliers, sample the rest at 5%, decided at the gateway collector tier. Ratified by three stewards after the restart-orphaning risk was verified in the lab; rolled out behind a per-service flag with StatsD parity dashboards.
Approved design · Observability Platform
Approved
Knowledge
110
See all 110
A batch processor with no queue limit is not backpressure, it's a memory leak waiting for a spike
The batch processor's default config has no size cap — under normal load that never shows, under a burst it's the difference between throttling and crashing.
Observation
A collector restart during a rolling deploy drops its in-flight batch silently
Rolling collector pods one at a time still loses whatever batch was buffered at restart; a graceful-drain hook is the fix, not yet clustered with the queue-limit work.
Observation
A decommission checklist per service prevents an alert going dark silently
One service's alerting rule referenced the StatsD metric directly; the checklist now requires re-pointing every alert before that service's StatsD emitter is removed.
Observation
A masquerading admin must not bump the target user’s epoch
Bumping on masquerade would log the impersonated user out of their own live sessions the moment an admin looked at the account.
Observation
A per-tenant Cognito client also isolates a misconfigured redirect to one tenant
When one tenant’s redirect URI was briefly wrong, only that tenant’s login broke — a shared client would have taken every tenant down together.
Observation
A per-tenant feature flag lets support flip a tenant back to SAML if the cutover misbehaves
Keeping the SAML shim reachable behind a flag, instead of deleting it per tenant, turned one early cutover bug into a five-minute rollback instead of an incident.
Observation
A service with no traffic reports a 0% error rate that means nothing
Burn-rate math divides by request volume; a dead service scores a perfect error rate right up until someone notices no requests are landing at all — added a floor on minimum traffic before burn-rate suppresses a raw-volume alert.
Observation
A teardown proposal names the floor it removes and the initiative it was billed to
The proposal template now requires both numbers up front, so an approver isn't chasing them down before they can say yes.
Observation
A trace that never closes pins memory in the tail sampler
A stuck downstream call held a trace open indefinitely; added a hard timeout so an incomplete trace still gets flushed and sampled on its partial data.
Observation
A warm-up SELECT 1 before the real query, plus 6x3s retry, clears the cold-start race
Retrying the same transient error six times with a 3-second backoff — after one throwaway warm-up query — reliably gets past the cold-start window.
Observation
Add session_epoch so a tenant/role switch can invalidate old cookies
A stateless signed cookie can't be revoked directly; bumping a stored epoch and rejecting any cookie below it closes the replay window within one refresh cycle.
Observation
Agents read their system prompt from Prompt Management on every invocation
A 60-second cache means a Prompt Studio edit reaches the deployed fleet in about a minute, with no image rebuild and no redeploy.
Observation
Alert on error-budget burn rate, not raw error count
Multi-window burn-rate alerts against each SLO catch both fast and slow outages, with a minimum-traffic floor so a dead service can’t look healthy.
Pattern
An LLM evaluator flags CSRF-weakening diffs before a human reviewer sees them
Running every auth-service PR diff through the CSRF evaluator catches token-check removals immediately, instead of relying on a reviewer to notice a missing check in a large diff.
Observation
Any Bedrock list API in this codebase must be paginated by convention, not by memory
This was the second list-truncation bug found the same way; the convention now gets called out explicitly in review for any new Bedrock list call.
Observation
Attach the role-specific guardrail at model-build time, not a single global one
